Nowogard Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Nowogard, Poland

Demolished. Until at least 1817, Nowogard's small Jewish community had no cemetery of its own, burying its dead instead in nearby Płoty, documented elsewhere in this collection, where a cemetery had operated since the second half of the 18th century. This cemetery was established following a land grant from municipal authorities; the local Jewish community grew from 69 members in 1849 to 108 by the century's end, supported by a synagogue built in the 1860s. During Kristallnacht in November 1938, the synagogue was burned, and the cemetery is presumed to have been destroyed along with it.
